anyOf.description: A receipt must carry at least one verifiable piece of evidence: a seller reference number, a screenshot hash, or a non-empty evidence-items list.

description: A shareable, public cancellation receipt. Version 0.2. Accepts receipts written as version 0.1 or 0.2. See CANCEL-PROOF-SPEC-v0.2.md. Receipts are public by design: they MUST NOT contain passwords, full account numbers, or payment details.

type.description: How the account is identified. Partial or hashed only — never a full identifier. For email_hash, v0.2 defines the value as the salted hash SHA-256(lowercased email + ":" + receipt_id); bare SHA-256(email) values from v0.1 are deprecated (spec section 4).

value.description: Partial identifier (e.g. am***@example.com) or, for email_hash, the salted SHA-256 hex. Absent when type is "none".

datetime_utc.description: When the cancellation was requested/registered, UTC, ISO 8601, Zulu form.

effective_at.description: When the cancellation takes effect, if different from datetime_utc (e.g. end of the paid period). A charge between datetime_utc and effective_at is legitimate. UTC, ISO 8601, Zulu form.

reference.description: Confirmation/reference number given by the seller, if any.

charges_after_cancel.description: Charges the seller placed after the cancellation. Used as chargeback/dispute evidence.

amount.description: Charge amount in major currency units (e.g. 29.99). Kept for v0.1 compatibility; at most 2 decimal places. New receipts SHOULD use amount_minor instead.

amount_minor.description: Charge amount in the smallest currency unit (e.g. 2999 for $29.99, 3000 for JPY 3000). Preferred over amount: exact integers, no float rounding.

currency.description: ISO 4217 currency code, e.g. USD, EUR.

date.description: Date of the charge (date only). Must be after the cancellation date.

created_utc.description: When this receipt file was created, UTC, ISO 8601, Zulu form.

items.description: Controlled vocabulary. Feeds the dark-pattern incident registry (phase 2).
Additional evidence items (confirmation email, PDF, seller response, ...). At least one item counts as evidence for the receipt.

hash.description: SHA-256 hash (lowercase hex) of the evidence file, if the item is a file.

received_utc.description: When this evidence was received, UTC, ISO 8601, Zulu form. A per-item timestamp from the seller's own message is stronger than the receipt's device clock.

ref.description: Reference number or identifier for this item, if it is not a file.

source.description: Where this evidence came from, e.g. "seller confirmation email".

screenshot_filename.description: Original filename of the screenshot, for the holder to find it again.

screenshot_sha256.description: SHA-256 hash (lowercase hex) of the screenshot file. The screenshot itself is NOT stored in the receipt.

issuer.description: Who issued the receipt. "consumer" for consumer-issued receipts; "seller" for sellers issuing receipts in this format (see MODEL-RULE-v0.2.md, Article 2).

notes.description: Optional free-text notes. No secrets, no personal data beyond what is needed.

receipt_id.description: Receipt identifier, e.g. CPR-2026-7K2Q9X4M. The year is the year the receipt was created. The suffix is 4-12 uppercase letters/digits; new receipts SHOULD use 8 characters generated from a cryptographic random source (spec section 4).

name.description: Service name as shown to the consumer.

signature.description: Optional seller signature (spec section 5). ECDSA P-256 (ES256) over the JCS canonical form (RFC 8785) of the receipt without this field. A signature proves the holder of the matching private key signed it; trust in the key comes from the key being published at the seller's domain.

algorithm.description: ECDSA P-256 with SHA-256 over the JCS canonical form.

key_url.description: Where the signer publishes this public key, e.g. https://seller.example/.well-known/cancel-proof-key.json. Readers SHOULD compare the embedded key against it.

public_key.description: The signer's P-256 public key as a JWK.

signature.description: Base64url (86 chars, no padding) of the 64-byte raw ECDSA signature (r || s, IEEE P1363).

status.description: Outcome of the cancellation dispute: the state of charges after cancellation. A receipt is a snapshot; a change of status goes in a superseding receipt (see superseded_by), not by editing this receipt.

date.description: Date the superseding receipt was issued (date only).

receipt_id.description: Receipt id of the superseding receipt.

superseded_by.description: Reference to the receipt that supersedes this one. A string is the v0.1 form (a receipt id); an object is the v0.2 form. Readers MUST accept both.

version.description: Format version. Version 0.1 receipts remain valid under this schema.

title: Cancel-Proof receipt
